lesson_title: Can You Take It Home in a Bag?
hook_text: Vetkoek, a haircut, airtime and a taxi ride. Only two of them fit in a bag.
clip_script: Saturday, R150, one busy street. Two vetkoek: you can hold them, take them home. Goods. Haircut: try putting that in a bag. The barber did something for you. Service. Oranges: goods. Data: you are paying the network to carry your messages. Service. Taxi ride: service. Now flip it. Mama Joyce makes vetkoek, so she is a producer. But at six a.m. she bought flour, so she was a consumer too. The barber buys her vetkoek at lunch: consumer. Everyone wears two hats. That is how money goes round and round.
visual_style: A whiteboard street with stalls, a barber's chair and a taxi; a shopping bag that accepts goods and bounces services back.
mood: Lively and street-smart, a Saturday morning walk.
pacing: Quick stall-to-stall sorting, then a slower two-hats reveal.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and list five goods and five services your family paid for this week.
